title: ZDI publishes 0-day advisory on PyTorch torch_save_to_dcp deserialization flaw
date_note: Coordinated public release date on the ZDI advisory.
geo_basis: location not stated by source; map pin is a placeholder
summary: Zero Day Initiative published ZDI-26-1059 (CVE-2026-136433) as a 0-day: deserialization of untrusted data in PyTorch's torch_save_to_dcp checkpoint conversion could let an attacker execute code as the current user, with a CVSS 3.0 score of 7.8. ZDI says it reported the issue on 2026-08-26 and the vendor rejected it as expected behavior on 2026-09-01. The page mentions no patch.
plain: ZDI says a checkpoint conversion tool in PyTorch can run attacker code when a user opens a malicious file. ZDI says the vendor treated it as expected behavior, and its page lists no patch.
exec: ZDI's advisory says the flaw lets code run as the current user when a malicious file is opened; its page lists no fix.
action: ZDI advises restricting interaction with the product; its page lists no patch.

validation.note: Only ZDI's advisory was read; the vendor's position is given as ZDI describes it.

review.note: Compared CVE, CVSS 7.8, timeline, vendor rejection, mitigation and 0-day wording with ZDI-26-1059
